answer.original_source: NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement; partner quotes from Sharon AI and Firmus relayed within the same post)
answer.new_information: NVIDIA said on 2026-07-01 it is introducing a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. Under the stated partnership, AI clouds would sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services, and NVIDIA would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. Supporting items in the same post: Sharon AI CEO James Manning called the collaboration a pivotal moment (party quote, no figures); NVIDIA said AI cloud companies are building DSX AI factories across regions (forecast-style, no count or date); Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs (expected plan, stated by NVIDIA, no completion date, no NVIDIA contract value or delivery timing). The credit-support amount, term, counterparties' commitments, revenue-share percentage and accounting treatment are not stated, so no quantified NVIDIA obligation or revenue is established. Firmus capacity is a partner plan, not NVIDIA revenue or orders.
answer.reason: Identified origin is NVIDIA itself, so this is the first identified origin for this claim and not corroboration. No matched catalog claim exists. A proposed question is warranted because the credit-support and revenue-share model may create guarantee or purchase-type obligations for NVIDIA, which are currently unquantified. Public evidence that would settle it: NVIDIA quarterly 10-Q and annual 10-K disclosures on guarantees, credit support, deferred revenue and cloud-linked revenue, plus any signed AI cloud agreements. Check date: next annual filing, with a signing check within 18 months. Nearest catalog question: none supplied. Folding into a generic AI demand question would lose the separate contingent-exposure and revenue-share question.

arguments.statement: The claim supports a conditional view only: NVIDIA's announced credit-support and revenue-sharing model could create a new NVIDIA guarantee or purchase-type exposure and a usage-linked revenue stream, but the amount, term and signing status are not established in the supplied text.
limitations: Source is NVIDIA's own blog post, a party statement with no independent verification.
No credit-support amount, guarantee cap, revenue-share percentage or contract duration is given.
Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are an expected partner plan, not NVIDIA revenue, orders or a signed obligation.
Sharon AI and other AI cloud statements are party quotes with no figures.
No catalog questions or stored pieces were supplied to compare against.
what_would_change_it: NVIDIA 10-Q or 10-K disclosure quantifying credit-support, guarantee or purchase commitments tied to AI cloud partners.
Signed agreements naming NVIDIA credit-support terms or revenue-share percentages with specific AI clouds.
Disclosure of cloud-linked revenue or deferred revenue separate from standard product revenue.
Evidence that the Firmus campus has signed NVIDIA supply or financing terms with stated timing.

answer.independent_judgement: Based only on NVIDIA's own 2026-07-01 statement, the model could add a recurring, usage-linked revenue component and a contingent credit-support exposure for NVDA, but neither is quantified or signed in the supplied text. The Firmus and Sharon AI items are partner plans and quotes that show intent, not NVDA revenue. Treat the claim as a lead to be checked against future filings and signed agreements, not as an established financial effect.
answer.new_question: Will NVIDIA disclose quantified credit-support, guarantee, purchase or revenue-share obligations tied to its AI cloud partner model in its next annual filing, or in signed agreements within 18 months of 2026-07-01?
